HOSPITAL COURSE

This is an ___ year old gentleman with a history of coronary 
artery disease, CABG, history of PEA arrest, systolic heart 
failure and second degree AV block with dual chamber pacemaker 
who presented with increasing dyspnea on exertion.

An excercise 
stress test demonstrated abnormal progressive drop in blood 
pressure with increasing excercise suggesting progressive 
disease.
ACTIVE ISSUES

# DYSPNEA: Chest xray at outside hospital prior to admission 
demonstrated vascular congestion consistent with rales 
auscultated on physical exam.

He was gently diuresed for aute 
decompensated congestive heart failure.

Cardiac enzymes were 
flat, troponin elevation likely reflected chronic renal 
disaease.
An echo demonstated reduced ejection fraction LVEF of

35% when compared to prior and moderate global left ventricular 
hypokinesis.

An excercise tolerance test demonstrated 
progressive drop in blood pressure with increasing excercise.
He was able to exercise for 4.25 of a Gervino protocol (~3.2

METs) and was stopped due to systolic blood pressure drop and 
symptoms of fatigue.

This poor performance on ETT was 
concerning for progression of coronary artery disease.

Given 
the patient's coronary anatomy status post CABG and findings on 
recent catherization, CABG was discussed with the patient and 
his family.

# CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE: History of significant coronary 
artery disease status post CABG in ___ with SVG to the OM and
RCA and LIMA to the LAD.

Most recent cathetrization in ___ 
demonstrated 3 vessel disease with occlusion of the SVGs to the

OM and RCA and patent LAD and mid vessel occlusion at the 
diagonal 1.

He was continued on aspirin, statin and isosorbide 
dinitrate.
Management as above.

# PUMP: History of systolic heart failure reflecting likely 
ischemic cardiomyopathy.
LVEF on TTE here 35%.

Management for 
mild decompensation as outlined above.

while inpatient.

exam.
# BPH: Stable.
He was continued on doxazosin.
# ANEMIA.
